ImageDescription.value: At the southeast end of Avenida da Liberdade, near Praca do Rossio, the popular name of Praça de D. Pedro IV and set on Praça dos Restauradores is the Monument to the Restorers (Monumento aos Restauradores). The monument was designed by António Tomás da Fonseca and erected in 1886; sculptors were Simões de Almeida and Alberto Nunes.  The obelisk carries the names and dates of the battles fought during the Portuguese Restoration War in 1640.

Categories.value: Palácio Foz|Flickr images missing SDC inception|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2

ImageDescription.value: The Inspecção Geral das Actividades Culturais building in Lisbon stands as a refined example of Portuguese Neoclassical architecture, blending symmetry, proportion, and decorative artistry. Its pastel pink facade, accented with crisp white stonework, Corinthian pilasters, and wrought-iron balconies, exudes elegance against the city’s brilliant blue skies. A central pediment crowned with sculptural figures adds grandeur, while the slate mansard roof evokes Parisian influence. Located in Lisbon’s historic heart, this landmark reflects the city’s dedication to preserving both cultural heritage and architectural beauty. A favorite for photographers and architecture lovers, it’s a striking emblem of Lisbon’s artistic and civic identity.
